profile.name: Deepti Sharma
profile.writeup:
The modern evolution of women's all-round cricket in India is defined by the ruthless, multi-dimensional utility of Deepti Sharma. Operating as a cunning off-spinner, an adaptable middle-order batter, and a sharp inner-ring fielder, Sharma dismantled the traditional boundary between specialised bowling and anchored batting. Born in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, her tactical philosophy centres on spatial awareness and relentless consistency. Rather than relying on exaggerated turn or brute power, she controls the tempo of matches through tight bowling lines, subtle changes of pace, and precise gap-finding with the bat.


Recognised globally as one of the premier all-rounders of her generation, Sharma has compiled an exceptional portfolio of individual accolades and landmark performances. In 2020, she was conferred with the prestigious Arjuna Award by the Government of India for her outstanding athletic contributions. Among her most iconic displays was her staggering 188 against Ireland in Potchefstroom in 2017, a marathon knock that shattered existing scoring benchmarks for Indian women's ODI cricket. In that same match, she partnered with Punam Raut in a monumental 320-run opening stand, demonstrating an extraordinary capacity to dictate play for an entire fifty-over innings.


Her impact across white-ball international cricket is anchored by unprecedented historical benchmarks. She became the first Indian woman bowler to claim 100 T20 International wickets and holds the distinction of being the first Indian woman cricketer to complete the rare double of 1,000 runs and 100 wickets in both ODIs and T20Is. Whether stalling Powerplay momentum with the new ball or navigating tight run-chases in the lower-middle order, her technical versatility makes her an indispensable tactical piece across all conditions.


Beyond her international dominance, Sharma has established herself as a cornerstone of elite global leagues, serving as a marquee all-rounder for UP Warriorz in the Women's Premier League. She played a pivotal role in India securing the gold medal at the Asian Games and was an essential contributor to India's historic 2025 ICC Women's ODI World Cup title victory. As an active player at the peak of her physical powers, Sharma continues to redefine the tactical standards for world-class all-rounders on the global stage.
